newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Thai oil export continues after low monsoon demand.
newsitem.headline: Thai oil export continues after low monsoon demand.

text.p: Thailand is not expected to cut its spot petroleum product exports even after the low demand monsoon season ends because refiners will raise output to take advantage of high international prices, sources said on Friday.

Thai refiners lowered refinery operating rates by 10 percent to 15 percent in October and November due to low domestic demand during the rainy season and high international crude oil prices, sources in Bangkok said.

The monsoon season lasts until late November, by which time domestic demand is projected to rise by about 10 percent. Some traders believed that Thailand would cease its oil product exports to meet this rising local demand, one Thai trader said.
But Thai refiners said they would not reduce exports despite the projections because refinery output in the country was expected to rise next month.
"The current high spot prices make it profitable to export," one refiner said. "So there is no need to maintain the run cut."

Thailand started regular monthly exports of two million to three million barrels of petroleum products such as gasoline, diesel and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) in the middle of this year after the start up of two new refineries.
The two new refineries added 275,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) of refining capacity, bringing total refining capacity to 760,000 bpd.

Emphasising Thailand's new role as an exporter, two refiners recently sealed for the first time one-year term contracts to export at least one 240,000-barrel gasoline cargo per quarter. A third refiner exports between 125,000 and 170,000 barrels of gasoline a month to Vietnam.
The refiners' export zeal is boosted by soaring oil product prices. Diesel traded at another five-year high this week.
As a result, the Thai refiners have recently sold their diesel and gasoline at a premium to Singapore spot quotes, compared to a discount to Singapore prices previously.
Its last gasoline sale was at 18 cents above Singapore spot quotes on a free-on-board (fob) basis, compared to a discount of about 70 cents for sales done in July, traders said.
Diesel sales have also seen similar increases, with its last sale a 20-cent premium to Singapore spot quotes on an fob basis, compared to a 60-cent discount in mid-August, traders said.

Among the refiners who were last reported to have operated below normal capacity are Esso (Thailand) PLC, an affiliate of U.S. oil giant Exxon Corp. Esso reduced runs at its 145,000-bpd refinery by 10 percent to 15 percent for the first time in October. Rayong Refinery Co is also operating its 145,000-bpd refinery at 80 percent to 85 percent of capacity.
Traders said the refiners are likely to restore production to full capacity during early December.
Rayong Refinery, a 60-40 joint venture between Royal Dutch Shell and state-owned Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT), is also aiding other refiners in their export efforts through product exchange.

In the third quarter, Rayong swapped jet fuel and diesel cargoes with Esso and Thai Oil Co Ltd, which involved the refiners taking the cargoes from Rayong for export and returning a similar cargo into Thailand.
